title: openai-compat: normalize tool schema mapping and tool_choice semantics, improve tool message formatting
author: Priya Shah
release_notes: OpenAI-compat: tool schema mapping normalization; explicit tool_choice semantics adoption; improved tool message formatting for deterministic downstream parsing
description:
Motivation: Bring Redwood's OpenAI compatibility layer for function/tool calling in line with the latest OpenAI tool schema expectations and tool_choice semantics used by downstream SDKs. This PR normalizes tool schema -> internal tool mapping, formalizes tool_choice handling (including explicit agented vs. assistant-invoked tool selection), and tidies the tool message formatting to ensure deterministic structured outputs for clients and evals. Changes summarized below.

Summary of changes: 1) tool schema mapping: added a canonical mapper that flattens 'properties' / 'required' / 'oneOf' patterns into the internal ToolSpec used by the compatibility layer, with defensive validation and helpful diagnostics on mismatch. 2) tool_choice semantics: introduced explicit support for OpenAI-style "tool_choice" objects in model responses (name/confidence/arguments), including backward-compatible handling for earlier assistant messages that only returned 'tool' strings. 3) tool message formatting: standardized the framing of tool invocation messages emitted by the API so that SDKs can reliably parse tool outputs (content-type, tool-metadata header, and JSON-schema-wrapped payload). 4) Streaming stability: fixed an edge case where partial tool_choice tokens could be emitted in separate chunks leading to invalid intermediate JSON; we now buffer until a complete top-level object is emitted for streaming consumers. 5) Tests/docs: added unit and integration tests and expanded the OpenAI-compat docs section with examples and migration notes.

Files changed (high-level): compat/openai/mapper.py, compat/openai/handler.py, compat/openai/streaming.py, sdk/python/openai_compat.py, docs/openai-tool-calling.md, tests/compat/test_tool_choice.py.

Testing and validation: Local unit tests cover mapping edge cases (oneOf, nested objects), tool_choice edge cases (missing confidence, ambiguous name resolution), and streaming reassembly. Integration tests run against the example model shim to validate streaming + tool invocation end-to-end. CI: lint -> pass, unit -> pass, integration -> pass after a flaky streaming test was stabilized.

Migration notes: No mandatory changes for customers using the Redwood API in the short term. SDKs will gradually surface the new tool_choice structure; customers that parse raw assistant text should prefer the structured tool invocation fields (tool.name and tool.arguments) going forward. See docs/openai-tool-calling.md for examples and a migration snippet for Python/TS SDKs.

Related: linear/ENG-2721, ENG-2808.
commits: 1) add canonical tool schema mapper and validation (sha: a1b2c3d); 2) implement tool_choice handling and backward compat (sha: b2c3d4e); 3) fix streaming JSON chunking for tool payloads (sha: c3d4e5f); 4) tests and docs (sha: d4e5f6a)
review_comments:
Arjun Patel: Please add a test for conflicting oneOf branches where both validate but pick by preference order - also document behavior.
Priya Shah: Added test and documented preference order in mapper docstring and docs/openai-tool-calling.md

Maya Liu: The streaming buffer change looks good but can you add a small benchmark to show we don't add measurable latency for small responses?
Priya Shah: Added microbenchmark in streaming.py and included results in the PR description; no measurable regression (median +0.2ms).

Diego Ramirez: Are there any security considerations for tool metadata headers? make sure we strip customer PII and don't leak internal model identifiers.
Priya Shah: Added header whitelist and sanitization step before emitting headers.
compatibility_notes: Backward-compatible: assistant-only 'tool' string responses are still accepted and mapped to tool_choice.name
Recommended: SDKs should consume explicit tool_choice objects when present to get confidence/arguments
Streaming consumers: expect complete JSON top-level objects for tool invocations; partial objects will not be emitted until complete
migration_steps: SDKs: bump openai-compat adapter minor version to expose tool_choice object
App developers parsing raw assistant text: prefer structured tool invocation fields when available
Operators: no config changes required unless you use custom tool metadata headers - see docs for header whitelist config
